transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Ramos (CTO - Cascade), Priya Kapoor (Head of Security - Cascade), Liam O'Neill (Platform Eng - Cascade)

Summary:
Brief discovery focused on Cascade's security posture requirements for evaluating Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key areas: SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML & SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS (BYOK), data residency and deletion/retention policies. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and certs, schedule benchmarks, customer to confirm residency constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood inference — i'm the account lead, and with me is maya our solutions engineer. quick check on audio?
[00:08] Evan (Cascade): good here, thanks. we have priya on, and liam as well. excited to dig in on security — this is pretty central for our evaluation.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood): great, hi all. our plan is to run through your high-level controls and then dig into any specific must-haves — soc 2, iso, sso, kms, that sort of list. feel free to stop and ask.
[00:28] Priya (Cascade): perfect. to set context; cascade handles financial reconciliation data for eu customers, so we have strict residency and audit requirements. our security bar includes SOC 2 Type II, iso 27001, sso via saml, scim for user provisioning, and cust-managed keys for any sensitive persisted customer data.

[00:45] Jordan (Redwood): understood. quick call-out on deployment options: we offer hosted api (fastest onboarding), dedicated reserved capacity (isolated infra but still managed by redwood), and private deployments (vpc/on-prem where you control networking and can bring your own kms/hsm).
[00:59] Liam (Cascade): when you say private, is that fully air-gapped on prem, or also vpc with peering? what's the typical model?
[01:07] Maya (Redwood): both. we do a private control plane option and an on-prem package for air-gapped customers. for most enterprise customers in eu we do VPC peering or private link into their cloud region, and for the highest-control customers we can ship an on-prem bundle — that includes the ability to integrate with your KMS/HSM.

[01:25] Evan (Cascade): ok, good. on compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports we can review? also, any third-party pen test results?
[01:34] Jordan (Redwood): yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. i'll send the certs and the security pack after the call — it includes pen test summaries, third-party attestation info, and an architecture diagram.
[01:43] Priya (Cascade): great — also need to understand audit logs: what events are logged, retention periods by default, can we export them to our SIEM?
[01:52] Maya (Redwood): we capture auth events, api requests/responses metadata, model/version used, policy decisions, and admin changes. Hosted default retention is 90 days for detailed logs, with longer retention available as an add-on. we support log forwarding via syslog/S3 ingestion to your SIEM; for dedicated or private deployments you can set retention to match your policy and keep logs in your environment.

[02:15] Liam (Cascade): syslog forwarding or S3 is fine. for dedicated, do you keep any persistent customer data? we want to make sure embeddings or request payloads aren't stored longer than needed.
[02:24] Maya (Redwood): by default, for hosted we retain request payloads for 30 days for billing and quality monitoring, but we offer an option to disable retention or reduce to 0 for paid enterprise plans. for dedicated and private, data stays in your environment and retention is under your control; in private on-prem you manage storage and can enforce deletion. note: for some debugging traces we may have ephemeral logs, but they can be disabled for strict compliance workloads.

[02:50] Priya (Cascade): what about key management? BYOK and HSM support? can keys be rotated without downtime?
[02:57] Maya (Redwood): we support KMS integrations across major cloud providers and offer BYOK for Dedicated and Private. HSM-backed keys are supported in private deployments. key rotation is supported and typically seamless — we do a staged rewrap that avoids downtime, but we'll provide a runbook and we can test rotation as part of the pilot.

[03:18] Jordan (Redwood): i'll note that for hosted customers we can do envelope encryption with a customer-managed key in KMS for additional control; full HSM BYOK is usually part of the private on-prem package.

[03:30] Evan (Cascade): SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. how mature is your SAML/SCIM support and RBAC?
[03:38] Maya (Redwood): we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning out of the box. RBAC supports role templates (admin, dev, auditor) and custom roles with fine-grained permissions for model operations, keys, and billing. Audit trails of role changes are logged. for dedicated/private we can integrate with your existing identity provider via a trust connection.

[03:59] Priya (Cascade): do you provide separation of duties? e.g., ops cannot access raw customer payloads unless specifically approved?
[04:06] Maya (Redwood): yes — on dedicated and private we can enforce separation of duties; access to raw payloads is restricted and logged. for hosted we have strict access controls and just-in-time access for engineering on a need basis with SSO and audit approvals. we can share our access control policy as part of the security pack.

[04:26] Liam (Cascade): auditors will ask for proof — can we get access to the SOC 2 report and a contact for compliance questions?
[04:33] Jordan (Redwood): absolutely — i'll include the SOC 2 Type II report and our compliance contact. we also provide an attestation letter for customers.

[04:43] Evan (Cascade): ok, on the topic of network isolation — do you support VPC peering, private link, or static egress ip addresses for allowlisting?
[04:51] Maya (Redwood): yes to all three. VPC peering and PrivateLink are supported for dedicated and private. For hosted we can provide static egress IPs or IP ranges for allowlisting; with dedicated there's typically a dedicated network egress that we can reserve.

[05:08] Priya (Cascade): data residency: some of our customers require EU-only processing and storage. can you guarantee that?
[05:14] Jordan (Redwood): we have cloud regions in eu and can pin processing and storage to those regions. for the strongest guarantee we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments in an eu region so storage never leaves eu. we'll need to capture exact residency requirements and SLAs as part of the contract.

[05:28] Liam (Cascade): good. one more on logging: what about cryptographic proof of deletion when we request data wipe?
[05:35] Maya (Redwood): we provide deletion confirmation and audit logs showing deletion events. for private/on-prem we can provide the deletion runbook and logs from your environment. For hosted we maintain an immutable audit trail showing deletion request, processing, and confirmation timestamps — we can include sample logs in the security pack.

[05:53] Evan (Cascade): product team question — how do you handle model rollouts and fallback? any chance of a degraded model being used accidentally and affecting production outputs?
[06:01] Maya (Redwood): our rollout system supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic rollback on quality/regression checks. you can pin routes to a model version; for critical traffic we recommend dedicated with pinned models and shadow testing. all rollouts are audited.

[06:18] Priya (Cascade): do you run internal red-team or adversarial evals on models for data leakage?
[06:24] Maya (Redwood): yes, we run regular privacy and leakage checks during model onboarding and before production rollouts. we also have a quality monitoring service that can alert on regression and potential leakage patterns.

[06:36] Jordan (Redwood): switching gears — pricing & contractual asks will matter; for host vs dedicated vs private we can provide an apples-to-apples cost comparison including additional compliance costs like extended log retention or BYOK.
[06:48] Evan (Cascade): timing — we aim to decide vendor and sign POC by end of quarter, so quick turnaround on docs would help.

[06:55] Jordan (Redwood): noted. we'll prioritize the SOC2/ISO docs and benchmark scheduling.

[07:00] Maya (Redwood): technical detail question for liam — for the benchmark, what's your avg sequence length and concurrency?
[07:06] Liam (Cascade): avg seqs are about 700 tokens, peak concurrency around 40 requests/sec for normal operations, bursts to 120 qps during month-end. embeddings workload is separate but smaller.

[07:18] Maya (Redwood): that helps; our runtime can be configured with continuous batching and kv cache to manage latency/cost tradeoffs. for burst capacity dedicated offers guaranteed headroom; private can be right-sized in your infra.

[07:32] Priya (Cascade): last thing — any certifications around encryption-at-rest & in-transit specifics? TLS versions, algorithm details?
[07:40] Jordan (Redwood): yes, we use TLS 1.2+ (1.3 preferred) for in-flight; at-rest we default to AES-256 with envelope encryption. KMS integrations use provider-native KMS (AES-256 keys) and HSM options when requested. full crypto spec will be in the pack.

[07:55] Evan (Cascade): sounds good. one small concern — for hosted, if you do request retention for quality monitoring, is that automatic or opt-in? we prefer opt-in.
[08:03] Maya (Redwood): opt-in for the longer retention; default for hosted is short-term retention, and extended retention or storing request payloads for longer is an opt-in enterprise setting.

[08:14] Jordan (Redwood): recap and next steps: i'll send the security pack (SOC2/ISO certs, pen test summary, architecture diagrams), maya will coordinate benchmarking options for dedicated/private, and liam/priya will confirm residency plus share infra diagram. we'll aim for the docs out by 2026-03-10.
[08:32] Priya (Cascade): thanks — that timeline works.
[08:36] Evan (Cascade): thanks everyone.
[08:38] Maya (Redwood): thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a link to the security pack.

End of transcript.
